title: When Can I Quit? Calculator
description: Explore the time to a savings target using an adjustable savings rate and return assumption. A planning scenario, not a safe-to-quit date.

inputs.name: effectiveTaxPercent
inputs.label: Estimated Effective Tax and Deduction Rate (%)

methodSummary: Monthly contribution = annual salary / 12 × (1 − effective deduction rate / 100) × savings rate / 100 + monthly side income saved.
Targets = monthly expenses × 6 and monthly expenses × 12 × 25.
Savings compound monthly at entered annual return / 12, with contributions at month end.
assumptions: The deduction percentage is your estimate, not a tax calculation.
All entered side income is saved after expenses and taxes.
Return and spending stay constant. Use zero return to inspect a cash-only scenario.
insights: At zero return, $10,000 savings and $1,000 monthly contributions reach an $18,000 target in eight months.
Lower spending reduces the target, but this calculator only changes contributions when you change the savings inputs.

richContent:
A cash-only example

With $10,000 already saved and monthly expenses of $3,000, the six-month reserve is $18,000. Saving $1,000 each month at zero return takes eight months to close the $8,000 gap. A $500 unexpected bill increases that gap; a delayed paycheck can change the timing.

Keep the two targets separate

A short career break and long-term retirement have different requirements. The 25× spending output is a scenario for accumulation, not a withdrawal simulation. It does not model investment losses, sequence of returns, future taxes or changing family costs.

Use the transition checklist to check insurance and one-time expenses. If a job loss has already happened, the layoff calculator separates benefit timing from available savings.
quickAnswer: A savings milestone is not permission to quit. Model an expense reserve, then test lower returns, higher expenses and delayed income.
resultNote: The six-month and 25× targets are illustrative. Constant returns omit volatility, fees, inflation and withdrawal risk; reaching 25× spending does not guarantee lifelong income.
